# Configure PVS Accelerator

Build a PVS Accelerator site from nothing and take it down again: introduce the site and a PVS server, put a read cache on each host's local storage, accelerate a VM by proxying its first NIC, then forget the site — which cascades to everything hanging off it.

Workflow `configure-pvs-accelerator`. [All workflows](README.md) · [Connecting](connecting.md)

## C# (.NET)

```csharp
private static void ConfigurePvsAccelerator(string url, string user, string password)
{
    var session = Connect(url, user, password);

    var site = PVS_site.introduce(session, "sdk-pvs-farm", "Created by the SDK examples", "");
    PVS_server.introduce(session, new[] { "10.62.0.90" }, 6910, 6930, site);

    // The read cache must be on LOCAL storage. The point of the accelerator is to keep reads off
    // the network, so a cache on a shared SR would defeat it and the server rejects one.
    foreach (var hostRef in Host.get_all(session))
    {
        var local = LocalSr(session, hostRef);
        if (local == null) continue;
        PVS_cache_storage.create(session, new PVS_cache_storage
        {
            host = new XenRef<Host>(hostRef.opaque_ref),
            SR = new XenRef<SR>(local),
            site = new XenRef<PVS_site>(site),
            size = 10L * 1024 * 1024 * 1024,
        });
    }

    // A proxy may only sit on the VM's LOWEST-numbered NIC, so sort by device rather than taking
    // VIFs[0] — the list comes back in creation order, which is the same thing only by luck.
    var vm = FirstUnacceleratedGuest(session);
    var vif = VM.get_VIFs(session, vm.opaque_ref)
        .OrderBy(r => int.Parse(VIF.get_device(session, r.opaque_ref)))
        .First();
    var proxy = PVS_proxy.create(session, site, vif.opaque_ref);

    var record = PVS_site.get_record(session, site);
    Console.WriteLine($"Site '{record.name_label}' with {record.cache_storage.Count} cache(s) "
                      + $"and {record.servers.Count} server(s)");
    // "caching" means it is actually accelerating. A site with no cache storage reports
    // "initialised", and a proxy on a VM whose NIC is unplugged reports "stopped".
    Console.WriteLine($"  {vm.name_label}: {PVS_proxy.get_status(session, proxy)}");

    // Forgetting the site only cascades its cache storage - a running proxy or a server it still has
    // makes forget refuse with PVS_SITE_CONTAINS_RUNNING_PROXIES/_SERVERS, so tear those down
    // ourselves first, in the same order every real PVS teardown uses.
    PVS_proxy.destroy(session, proxy);
    foreach (var serverRef in PVS_site.get_servers(session, site)) PVS_server.forget(session, serverRef.opaque_ref);
    PVS_site.forget(session, site);
    Console.WriteLine("OK: configure-pvs-accelerator");
    session.logout();
}
// Run it:
//   ConfigurePvsAccelerator("https://xenserver", "root", password);

/// <summary>The host's own non-ISO storage, found through its PBDs.</summary>
private static string LocalSr(Session session, XenRef<Host> host)
{
    foreach (var pbdRef in Host.get_PBDs(session, host.opaque_ref))
    {
        // Keep the REF and read the record through it: a record fetched by get_record does not
        // carry its own opaque_ref, so reaching for sr.opaque_ref afterwards hands you a null.
        var srRef = PBD.get_SR(session, pbdRef.opaque_ref);
        var sr = SR.get_record(session, srRef.opaque_ref);
        if (!sr.shared && sr.content_type != "iso" && sr.type != "udev")
            return srRef.opaque_ref;
    }
    return null;
}

/// <summary>
/// A running guest with a NIC that no proxy already covers. A VIF can carry only one proxy, so a VM
/// the pool already accelerates fails with PVS_PROXY_ALREADY_PRESENT.
/// </summary>
private static VM FirstUnacceleratedGuest(Session session)
{
    var taken = new HashSet<string>();
    foreach (var proxyRef in PVS_proxy.get_all(session))
    {
        var vifRef = PVS_proxy.get_VIF(session, proxyRef.opaque_ref);
        taken.Add(VIF.get_VM(session, vifRef.opaque_ref).opaque_ref);
    }
    foreach (var kv in VM.get_all_records(session))
    {
        var v = kv.Value;
        if (v.is_a_template || v.is_control_domain || v.is_a_snapshot) continue;
        if (v.power_state != vm_power_state.Running || v.VIFs.Count == 0) continue;
        if (taken.Contains(kv.Key.opaque_ref)) continue;
        v.opaque_ref = kv.Key.opaque_ref;
        return v;
    }
    throw new Exception("no unaccelerated running guest with a NIC");
}
```

## Python

```python
def configure_pvs_accelerator(url, username, password):
    """Build a PVS Accelerator site from nothing: a site, a PVS server, a read cache on each
    host, and one accelerated VM. Then take it all down again.

    The inventory example above reads a configuration someone else made; this one makes it."""
    session = connect(url, username, password)
    x = session.xenapi

    site = x.PVS_site.introduce("sdk-pvs-farm", "Created by the SDK examples", "")
    x.PVS_server.introduce(["10.62.0.90"], 6910, 6930, site)

    # The read cache must be on LOCAL storage. The point of the accelerator is to keep reads off
    # the network, so a cache on a shared SR would defeat it and xapi rejects one.
    for host in x.host.get_all():
        local = local_sr(x, host)
        if local:
            # size as a STRING: XML-RPC only carries 32-bit integers, so the Python binding passes
            # every XenAPI Int as a string. 10 GiB does not fit, and passing an int raises inside
            # xmlrpc.client rather than at the API — a confusing place to land.
            x.PVS_cache_storage.create({"host": host, "SR": local, "site": site,
                                        "size": str(10 * 1024 ** 3)})

    # A proxy may only sit on the VM's LOWEST-numbered VIF, so sort by device rather than taking
    # VIFs[0] — the list comes back in creation order, which is the same thing only by luck.
    vm = first_unaccelerated_guest(x)
    vifs = sorted(x.VM.get_VIFs(vm), key=lambda v: int(x.VIF.get_device(v)))
    proxy = x.PVS_proxy.create(site, vifs[0])

    print("Site '%s' with %d cache(s) and %d server(s)"
          % (x.PVS_site.get_name_label(site),
             len(x.PVS_site.get_cache_storage(site)),
             len(x.PVS_site.get_servers(site))))
    # "caching" means it is actually accelerating. A site with no cache storage reports
    # "initialised", and a proxy on a VM whose VIF is unplugged reports "stopped".
    print("  %s: %s" % (x.VM.get_name_label(vm), x.PVS_proxy.get_status(proxy)))

    # Forgetting the site only cascades its cache storage - a running proxy or a server it still
    # has makes forget refuse with PVS_SITE_CONTAINS_RUNNING_PROXIES/_SERVERS, so tear those down
    # ourselves first, in the same order every real PVS teardown uses.
    x.PVS_proxy.destroy(proxy)
    for server_ref in x.PVS_site.get_servers(site):
        x.PVS_server.forget(server_ref)
    x.PVS_site.forget(site)
    print("OK: configure-pvs-accelerator")
    session.logout()


def local_sr(x, host):
    """The host's own non-ISO storage, found through its PBDs."""
    for pbd in x.host.get_PBDs(host):
        sr = x.PBD.get_SR(pbd)
        record = x.SR.get_record(sr)
        if not record["shared"] and record["content_type"] != "iso" and record["type"] != "udev":
            return sr
    return None


def first_unaccelerated_guest(x):
    """A running guest with a NIC that no proxy already covers.

    A VIF can carry only one proxy, so a VM the pool already accelerates fails with
    PVS_PROXY_ALREADY_PRESENT — and the pool may well have been configured before this ran."""
    taken = set()
    for proxy in x.PVS_proxy.get_all():
        taken.add(x.VIF.get_VM(x.PVS_proxy.get_VIF(proxy)))
    for ref, vm in x.VM.get_all_records().items():
        if (not vm["is_a_template"] and not vm["is_control_domain"] and not vm["is_a_snapshot"]
                and vm["power_state"] == "Running" and vm["VIFs"] and ref not in taken):
            return ref
    raise Exception("no unaccelerated running guest with a NIC")


# Run it:
#   configure_pvs_accelerator("https://xenserver", "root", password)
```

## Java

```java
private static void configurePvsAccelerator(String url, String user, String password) throws Exception {
    Connection conn = connect(url, user, password);
    try {
        PVSSite site = PVSSite.introduce(conn, "sdk-pvs-farm", "Created by the SDK examples", "");
        PVSServer.introduce(conn, new java.util.HashSet<>(java.util.Arrays.asList("10.62.0.90")),
            6910L, 6930L, site);

        // The read cache must be on LOCAL storage. The point of the accelerator is to keep reads off
        // the network, so a cache on a shared SR would defeat it and the server rejects one.
        for (Host host : Host.getAll(conn)) {
            SR local = localSr(conn, host);
            if (local == null) continue;
            PVSCacheStorage.Record cache = new PVSCacheStorage.Record();
            cache.host = host;
            cache.SR = local;
            cache.site = site;
            cache.size = 10L * 1024 * 1024 * 1024;
            PVSCacheStorage.create(conn, cache);
        }

        // A proxy may only sit on the VM's LOWEST-numbered NIC, so sort by device rather than taking
        // the first VIF — the set comes back unordered, so "the first one" means nothing here.
        Map.Entry<VM, VM.Record> guest = firstUnacceleratedGuest(conn);
        VIF first = null;
        int lowest = Integer.MAX_VALUE;
        for (VIF vif : guest.getValue().VIFs) {
            int device = Integer.parseInt(vif.getDevice(conn));
            if (device < lowest) { lowest = device; first = vif; }
        }
        PVSProxy proxy = PVSProxy.create(conn, site, first);

        PVSSite.Record record = site.getRecord(conn);
        System.out.printf("Site '%s' with %d cache(s) and %d server(s)%n",
            record.nameLabel, record.cacheStorage.size(), record.servers.size());
        // "caching" means it is actually accelerating. A site with no cache storage reports
        // "initialised", and a proxy on a VM whose NIC is unplugged reports "stopped".
        System.out.printf("  %s: %s%n", guest.getValue().nameLabel, proxy.getStatus(conn));

        // Forgetting the site only cascades its cache storage - a running proxy or a server it still
        // has makes forget refuse with PVS_SITE_CONTAINS_RUNNING_PROXIES/_SERVERS, so tear those down
        // ourselves first, in the same order every real PVS teardown uses.
        proxy.destroy(conn);
        for (PVSServer server : site.getServers(conn)) server.forget(conn);
        site.forget(conn);
        System.out.println("OK: configure-pvs-accelerator");
    } finally {
        Session.logout(conn);
    }
}
// Run it:
//   configurePvsAccelerator("https://xenserver", "root", password);

/** The host's own non-ISO storage, found through its PBDs. */
private static SR localSr(Connection conn, Host host) throws Exception {
    for (PBD pbd : host.getPBDs(conn)) {
        SR sr = pbd.getSR(conn);
        SR.Record r = sr.getRecord(conn);
        if (!r.shared && !"iso".equals(r.contentType) && r.type != null && !r.type.equals("udev"))
            return sr;
    }
    return null;
}

/**
 * A running guest with a NIC that no proxy already covers. A VIF can carry only one proxy, so a VM
 * the pool already accelerates fails with PVS_PROXY_ALREADY_PRESENT.
 */
private static Map.Entry<VM, VM.Record> firstUnacceleratedGuest(Connection conn) throws Exception {
    java.util.Set<String> taken = new java.util.HashSet<>();
    for (PVSProxy proxy : PVSProxy.getAll(conn))
        taken.add(proxy.getVIF(conn).getVM(conn).toWireString());
    for (Map.Entry<VM, VM.Record> e : VM.getAllRecords(conn).entrySet()) {
        VM.Record v = e.getValue();
        if (v.isATemplate || v.isControlDomain || v.isASnapshot) continue;
        if (v.powerState != Types.VmPowerState.RUNNING || v.VIFs.isEmpty()) continue;
        if (taken.contains(e.getKey().toWireString())) continue;
        return e;
    }
    throw new Exception("no unaccelerated running guest with a NIC");
}
```

## Go

```go
func configurePvsAccelerator(url, user, password string) {
	session := connect(url, user, password)
	defer session.Logout()

	site, err := xenapi.PVSSite.Introduce(session, "sdk-pvs-farm", "Created by the SDK examples", "")
	check(err)
	_, err = xenapi.PVSServer.Introduce(session, []string{"10.62.0.90"}, 6910, 6930, site)
	check(err)

	// The read cache must be on LOCAL storage. The point of the accelerator is to keep reads off the
	// network, so a cache on a shared SR would defeat it and the server rejects one.
	hosts, err := xenapi.Host.GetAll(session)
	check(err)
	for _, host := range hosts {
		local, ok := localSR(session, host)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		_, err = xenapi.PVSCacheStorage.Create(session, xenapi.PVSCacheStorageRecord{
			Host: host, SR: local, Site: site, Size: 10 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024,
		})
		check(err)
	}

	// A proxy may only sit on the VM's LOWEST-numbered NIC, so sort by device rather than taking
	// VIFs[0] — the list comes back in creation order, which is the same thing only by luck.
	vm := firstUnacceleratedGuest(session)
	vifs := append([]xenapi.VIFRef(nil), vm.VIFs...)
	sort.Slice(vifs, func(i, j int) bool { return vifDevice(session, vifs[i]) < vifDevice(session, vifs[j]) })
	proxy, err := xenapi.PVSProxy.Create(session, site, vifs[0])
	check(err)

	record, err := xenapi.PVSSite.GetRecord(session, site)
	check(err)
	fmt.Printf("Site '%s' with %d cache(s) and %d server(s)\n",
		record.NameLabel, len(record.CacheStorage), len(record.Servers))
	// "caching" means it is actually accelerating. A site with no cache storage reports "initialised",
	// and a proxy on a VM whose NIC is unplugged reports "stopped".
	status, err := xenapi.PVSProxy.GetStatus(session, proxy)
	check(err)
	fmt.Printf("  %s: %s\n", vm.NameLabel, status)

	// Forgetting the site only cascades its cache storage - a running proxy or a server it still
	// has makes forget refuse with PVS_SITE_CONTAINS_RUNNING_PROXIES/_SERVERS, so tear those down
	// ourselves first, in the same order every real PVS teardown uses. (Cache storage doesn't need
	// a separate call - forget cascades it correctly.)
	check(xenapi.PVSProxy.Destroy(session, proxy))
	servers, err := xenapi.PVSSite.GetServers(session, site)
	check(err)
	for _, server := range servers {
		check(xenapi.PVSServer.Forget(session, server))
	}
	check(xenapi.PVSSite.Forget(session, site))
	fmt.Println("OK: configure-pvs-accelerator")
}

// localSR returns the host's own non-ISO storage, found through its PBDs.
func localSR(session *xenapi.Session, host xenapi.HostRef) (xenapi.SRRef, bool) {
	pbds, err := xenapi.Host.GetPBDs(session, host)
	check(err)
	for _, pbd := range pbds {
		ref, err := xenapi.PBD.GetSR(session, pbd)
		check(err)
		sr, err := xenapi.SR.GetRecord(session, ref)
		check(err)
		if !sr.Shared && sr.ContentType != "iso" && sr.Type != "udev" {
			return ref, true
		}
	}
	return "", false
}

func vifDevice(session *xenapi.Session, vif xenapi.VIFRef) int {
	device, err := xenapi.VIF.GetDevice(session, vif)
	check(err)
	n, _ := strconv.Atoi(device)
	return n
}

// firstUnacceleratedGuest returns a running guest with a NIC that no proxy already covers. A VIF can
// carry only one proxy, so a VM the pool already accelerates fails with PVS_PROXY_ALREADY_PRESENT.
func firstUnacceleratedGuest(session *xenapi.Session) xenapi.VMRecord {
	taken := map[xenapi.VMRef]bool{}
	proxies, err := xenapi.PVSProxy.GetAll(session)
	check(err)
	for _, proxy := range proxies {
		vif, err := xenapi.PVSProxy.GetVIF(session, proxy)
		check(err)
		vm, err := xenapi.VIF.GetVM(session, vif)
		check(err)
		taken[vm] = true
	}
	vms, err := xenapi.VM.GetAllRecords(session)
	check(err)
	for ref, v := range vms {
		if v.IsATemplate || v.IsControlDomain || v.IsASnapshot || taken[ref] {
			continue
		}
		if v.PowerState == xenapi.VMPowerStateRunning && len(v.VIFs) > 0 {
			return v
		}
	}
	panic("no unaccelerated running guest with a NIC")
}
```

## PowerShell

```powershell
function Invoke-ConfigurePvsAccelerator {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Url,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$UserName,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Password
    )
    $session = Connect-Example -Url $Url -UserName $UserName -Password $Password

    # PVS_site.introduce and PVS_server.introduce are CONSTRUCTORS, and every parameter set of
    # Invoke-XenPVSSite / Invoke-XenPVSServer identifies an object that ALREADY EXISTS (-PVSSite / -Ref /
    # -Uuid / -Name). Introduce is in the -XenAction enum, but there is no way to call it: name an object
    # and it goes looking for one that isn't there yet; name none and PowerShell cannot choose between
    # four sets, so it fails at binding with AmbiguousParameterSet before the call is even attempted.
    # Same shape as Cluster.pool_create in configure-clustering — so, same answer: call the method over
    # JSON-RPC. Still pure PowerShell; no [XenAPI.*]:: statics.
    $site = Invoke-XenMethod -Session $session -Method 'PVS_site.introduce' `
        -Params @('sdk-pvs-farm', 'Created by the SDK examples', '')
    Invoke-XenMethod -Session $session -Method 'PVS_server.introduce' `
        -Params @(@('10.62.0.90'), 6910, 6930, $site) | Out-Null

    # The read cache must be on LOCAL storage: keeping reads off the network is the point, so a cache on
    # a shared SR would defeat it and the server rejects one. New-XenPVSCacheStorage is a real cmdlet.
    foreach ($xenHost in Get-XenHost) {
        $local = Get-XenPBD | Where-Object { $_.host.opaque_ref -eq $xenHost.opaque_ref } |
            ForEach-Object { Get-XenSR -Ref $_.SR.opaque_ref } |
            Where-Object { -not $_.shared -and $_.content_type -ne 'iso' -and $_.type -ne 'udev' } |
            Select-Object -First 1
        if (-not $local) { continue }
        New-XenPVSCacheStorage -XenHost $xenHost.opaque_ref -SR $local.opaque_ref -Site $site `
            -Size 10GB | Out-Null
    }

    # A proxy may only sit on the VM's LOWEST-numbered NIC, so sort by device rather than taking the
    # first VIF — the list comes back in creation order, which is the same thing only by luck.
    $accelerated = @(Get-XenPVSProxy | ForEach-Object { (Get-XenVIF -Ref $_.VIF.opaque_ref).VM.opaque_ref })
    $vm = Get-XenVM | Where-Object {
        -not $_.is_a_template -and -not $_.is_control_domain -and -not $_.is_a_snapshot -and
        $_.power_state -eq 'Running' -and $_.VIFs.Count -gt 0 -and $accelerated -notcontains $_.opaque_ref
    } | Select-Object -First 1
    $vif = $vm.VIFs | ForEach-Object { Get-XenVIF -Ref $_.opaque_ref } |
        Sort-Object { [int]$_.device } | Select-Object -First 1
    $proxy = New-XenPVSProxy -Site $site -VIF $vif.opaque_ref -PassThru

    $record = Get-XenPVSSite -Ref $site
    Write-Host "Site '$($record.name_label)' with $($record.cache_storage.Count) cache(s) and $($record.servers.Count) server(s)"
    # "caching" means it is really accelerating: a site with no cache reports "initialised", and a proxy
    # on a VM whose NIC is unplugged reports "stopped".
    Write-Host "  $($vm.name_label): $($proxy.status)"

    # Forgetting the site only cascades its cache storage - a running proxy or a server it still has
    # makes forget refuse with PVS_SITE_CONTAINS_RUNNING_PROXIES/_SERVERS, so tear those down ourselves
    # first, in the same order every real PVS teardown uses. (Cache storage doesn't need a separate
    # call - forget cascades it correctly.)
    Remove-XenPVSProxy -Ref $proxy.opaque_ref
    foreach ($serverRef in (Get-XenPVSSite -Ref $site).servers) {
        Invoke-XenPVSServer -Ref $serverRef.opaque_ref -XenAction Forget
    }
    Invoke-XenPVSSite -Ref $site -XenAction Forget
    Write-Host "OK: configure-pvs-accelerator"
    $session | Disconnect-XenServer
}
# Run it:
#   Invoke-ConfigurePvsAccelerator -Url https://xenserver -UserName root -Password $password
```

## xe CLI

```bash
w_configure_pvs_accelerator() {
    site=$(xe pvs-site-introduce name-label=sdk-pvs-farm name-description="Created by the SDK examples")
    xe pvs-server-introduce addresses=10.62.0.90 first-port=6910 last-port=6930 pvs-site-uuid="$site" >/dev/null

    # The read cache must be on LOCAL storage: keeping reads off the network is the point, so a cache
    # on a shared SR would defeat it and the server rejects one.
    for h in $(each_csv "$(xe host-list --minimal)"); do
        for pbd in $(each_csv "$(xe pbd-list host-uuid=$h --minimal)"); do
            sr=$(xe pbd-param-get uuid=$pbd param-name=sr-uuid)
            [ "$(xe sr-param-get uuid=$sr param-name=shared)" = "false" ] || continue
            [ "$(xe sr-param-get uuid=$sr param-name=content-type)" = "iso" ] && continue
            xe pvs-cache-storage-create uuid=$h sr-uuid=$sr pvs-site-uuid="$site" size=10737418240 >/dev/null
            break
        done
    done

    # A proxy may only sit on the VM's LOWEST-numbered NIC, and only one proxy may sit on a NIC — so
    # skip VMs the pool already accelerates and sort what is left by device.
    taken=""
    for proxy in $(each_csv "$(xe pvs-proxy-list --minimal)"); do
        vif=$(xe pvs-proxy-param-get uuid=$proxy param-name=vif-uuid)
        taken="$taken $(xe vif-param-get uuid=$vif param-name=vm-uuid)"
    done
    for vm in $(each_csv "$(xe vm-list power-state=running is-control-domain=false --minimal)"); do
        case "$taken" in *"$vm"*) continue ;; esac
        vif=$(xe vif-list vm-uuid=$vm params=uuid,device --minimal | sort_by_device)
        [ -n "$vif" ] || continue
        proxy=$(xe pvs-proxy-create pvs-site-uuid="$site" vif-uuid="$vif")
        name=$(xe vm-param-get uuid=$vm param-name=name-label)
        break
    done

    # Scoped to THIS site: the pool may already have one, and counting pool-wide would report its
    # caches and servers as though this example had made them.
    caches=$(count_csv "$(xe pvs-cache-storage-list pvs-site-uuid="$site" --minimal)")
    servers=$(count_csv "$(xe pvs-server-list pvs-site-uuid="$site" --minimal)")
    echo "Site '$(xe pvs-site-param-get uuid=$site param-name=name-label)' with $caches cache(s) and $servers server(s)"
    # "caching" means it is really accelerating: a site with no cache reports "initialised", and a
    # proxy on a VM whose NIC is unplugged reports "stopped".
    echo "  $name: $(xe pvs-proxy-param-get uuid=$proxy param-name=status)"

    # Forgetting the site only cascades its cache storage - a running proxy or a server it still has makes
    # forget refuse with PVS_SITE_CONTAINS_RUNNING_PROXIES/_SERVERS, so tear those down first, in the same
    # order every real PVS teardown uses.
    xe pvs-proxy-destroy uuid="$proxy"
    for srv in $(each_csv "$(xe pvs-server-list pvs-site-uuid="$site" --minimal)"); do
        xe pvs-server-forget uuid="$srv"
    done
    xe pvs-site-forget uuid="$site"
    echo "OK: configure-pvs-accelerator"
}

# Read "uuid,device,uuid,device,..." pairs on stdin and echo the uuid with the lowest device. Bash
# builtins only: on Windows every pipe stage is a process launch, and this runs once per VM.
sort_by_device() {
    local pairs best_uuid="" best_dev=""
    read -r pairs
    local IFS=,; set -- $pairs
    while [ $# -ge 2 ]; do
        if [ -z "$best_dev" ] || [ "$2" -lt "$best_dev" ]; then best_uuid=$1; best_dev=$2; fi
        shift 2
    done
    echo "$best_uuid"
}
```
